A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GraphGini and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification and fairness experiments on Credit, Income, and Pokec-n, including backbone comparisons, cluster analyses, and a GradNorm ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments on these datasets and reports additional baseline comparisons, fairness measurements, ablations, robustness tests, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The reported group-fairness loss changes from a sum over group pairs in v1 Section 3.3 to an average with factor 1/[m(m-1)] in v2. The backbone initialization, similarity-weighted attention, individual-fairness regularizer, and GradNorm procedure remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The three node-classification datasets remain unchanged, but v2 Appendices N–O add evaluation on graphs with controlled homophily and Gaussian-corrupted node features, substantially extending structural and input conditions. Appendix P describes existing group imbalance rather than introducing new populations or a controlled imbalance sweep.

E2.justification: The corresponding backbone comparisons expand from five fairness baselines to eleven, adding PostProcess, GNN GEI, iFairNMTF, TF-GNN, BeMAP, and FairSIN. v2 additionally evaluates REDRESS in Table Q and softmax/top-k regularizers in Tables N–P; these are evaluated comparisons, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: v2 adds F1 and Equal Opportunity evaluation and explicit IF-Gini/GD-Gini measurements in the main comparisons. New experiments introduce regularizer-removal controls, embedding dimensions 8/16/32, controlled rewiring and noise levels, and runtime measurement. The original training sample counts and validation/test proportions are retained.

E4.justification: The GradNorm ablation expands from Credit/GCN to all three datasets and backbones. v2 adds attention removal, separate fairness-regularizer removal, pooling-surrogate comparisons, weight and embedding-dimension sensitivity, and controlled structural/noise robustness analyses. These substantially extend the questions tested beyond v1's architecture, similarity-matrix, and limited GradNorm studies.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are repeated five times and report averages with standard deviations: v1 Section 4 and v2 Appendix H. No new seed disclosure, confidence-interval procedure, or significance test is introduced; additional result rows extend existing reporting practices.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline, metric, ablation, robustness, and runtime results. Retained benchmark values also change: Income/GCN GraphGini IF is 20.50±3.10 in v1 Table 2 and 21.12±5.22 in v2 Table 3, in thousands. However, v2 Table 5 attributes 21.12±5.22 to the variant without GradNorm, preventing a clean interpretation of this numerical revision. Most existing cluster scores are retained with rounding in Table L, alongside new F1 results.

T1.justification: v2 adds a Lipschitz counterexample, an Equal Opportunity definition and argument, a proposition asserting shared Gini/surrogate minimizers, a convexity proof, convergence and complexity analysis, and Appendix K's distributional bounds. It also replaces cumulative group disparity with average disparity. The existing Pareto-optimality argument is largely retained and moved to Appendix F, rather than newly established.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes introducing Gini-based joint fairness and eliminating manual loss-weight tuning. v2 makes Gini's claimed superiority over Lipschitz measures and promotion of Equal Opportunity headline contributions, while foregrounding the existing Pareto claim. Its conclusion softens eliminating manual tuning to mitigating extensive manual tuning.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning full-distribution fairness, outlier sensitivity, attention, GradNorm's treatment of differently scaled losses, and interactions between fairness regularizers. Appendices O and Q identify deterioration under stronger feature noise and larger embeddings, while Appendix P interprets performance on existing imbalanced groups.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, specifies one hidden layer of width 16, documents adaptations and hyperparameters for additional baselines, and supplies procedures for the new perturbation and sensitivity experiments. Hardware and original splits are retained. Conversely, v1's explicit fixed weights for the no-GradNorm ablation are no longer stated.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens positioning through additional fairness approaches, recent joint-fairness work by Wang and Yan, Equal Opportunity literature, and convergence literature. It explicitly acknowledges the Laplacian regularizer as an existing InFoRM heuristic and positions its contribution as a Gini-based interpretation. BeMAP's publication update alone does not constitute a new cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and introductory motivation are extensively rewritten. Background material is reorganized around individual and group fairness, while pseudocode, baseline descriptions, proofs, and existing analyses are redistributed into dedicated appendices. This changes the narrative structure beyond simply adding experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column conference layout to a single-column journal layout. v1 Table 2 is split into v2 Tables 3, 4, and M with additional metric columns and highlighted rows; the cluster table and weight trajectories move to the appendix. Numerous new tables, attention bar charts, benchmark bar charts, and sensitivity plots are added.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's limited comparative and diagnostic evidence through broader baselines, robustness tests, and reproducibility information. However, its main and GradNorm-ablation tables inconsistently attribute GraphGini scores. Its new motivating example also conflicts with its formula: Table 1 and Eq. 3, using the stated pairwise distance 2, yield Gini values approximately 0.382 and 0.370 rather than the claimed 0.377 and 0.74. These empirical and theoretical reliability concerns make the net quality benefit of the substantial additions uncertain.
